claims.text: 2023 annual real GDP growth was 2.5 percent, measured from the 2022 annual level to the 2023 annual level, up from 1.9 percent in 2022.

citations.quotation: Real GDP increased 2.5 percent in 2023 (from the 2022 annual level to the 2023 annual level), compared with an increase of 1.9 percent in 2022

claims.text: Quarterly figures are reported as annualized quarter-over-quarter rates: Q4 2023 grew at 3.3 percent and Q3 2023 at 4.9 percent. These quarterly annualized rates measure the pace within each quarter, whereas the 2.5 percent annual figure is a full-year (annual-level to annual-level) growth rate, so they are not directly comparable and quarterly rates can differ substantially from the annual rate.

citations.quotation: Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 3.3 percent in the fourth quarter of 2023
In the third quarter, real GDP increased 4.9 percent.
Real GDP increased 2.5 percent in 2023 (from the 2022 annual level to the 2023 annual level)

counterarguments.text: The source is the advance estimate, explicitly based on incomplete data subject to revision, so both the 2.5 percent annual and 3.3 percent quarterly figures could be revised.
The text does not fully explain the methodology linking quarterly annualized rates to the annual figure, so any explanation of their relationship beyond quoting the two measures is inference.

limitations: Supplied text does not include the full-year-to-year methodology definition beyond 'from the 2022 annual level to the 2023 annual level'.
No later revised estimates are provided; only the advance estimate is available.
The 4.2 percent vs 4.0 percent saving rate and 1.9 percent 2022 figure are contextual and not needed to answer the core question.
